title: PG-W-21F Trust proposal step: agents propose a grant or revocation as a decision, the person or operator answers, and the signed answer is the only way a trust record is written (memev, provisional under ADR 5)
request: Contract PG-W-21F in memev: the proposal step for trust changes under ADR 8, work package WP21-F1. Unsigned: a spec proposed for red-team review, PROVISIONAL under ADR 5. ORIGIN. The owner answered ADR 8 on 1 Nov 2026. Question 6: only a person or an operator grants or revokes trust; agents propose, the person approves, and the result is signed and logged. Clarification 5: the proposal step goes through the decision workflow of SO-A-05, and GRANT_AUTHORITY stays provisional under ADR 5. WHAT IT BUILDS. (1) src/engine/federation/trust-propose.mjs: proposeTrustChange makes a trust proposal (a grant or a revocation) as a decision of the decision queue of SO-A-05, with the proposer taken from a resolved actor and never from a field of the proposal, the proposed change validated by the record validator of PG-W-21A.2 without writing anything, a recommendation stored only in the recommendation field, no personal scope and no delegation block accepted; it has no trust book as an argument and so can never write trust. answerTrustChange lets only a person or an operator answer (the one frozen table GRANT_AUTHORITY of PG-W-21B, reused and not repeated; provisional under ADR 5), binds the answer to the hash of the exact change the person saw, has the person sign it (the person's signed act, in the namespace memev-trust-approval), calls the trust book to grant or revoke with the approver as the resolved actor, and appends an audit event; a rejection or a deferral writes no trust record. (2) src/engine/project-store.mjs: the decision entity of SO-A-05 gains two kinds, trust.grant and trust.revoke, in its closed kind list, and nothing else of the store changes. WHY THE PROPOSER CANNOT ANSWER FOR THE PERSON. A trust record names who is trusted for what; an agent that could write one would grant itself or another agent trust. The record is therefore written by the book only on the answer of a person or operator, the issuer of the record is that approver and not the proposer, the answer is explicit (no code path copies a recommendation into an answer, the rule of SO-A-05), and an edited or stale proposal cannot be approved because the approval covers its hash and a proposal not answered within 14 days is no longer approvable. DESIGN DECISIONS FOR THE RED-TEAM. (a) The decision queue is reached through a port { raise, read, settle } that the caller gives, an adapter over the SO-A-05 build; the module does not import the store, so the contract does not depend on names the SO-A-05 build has not fixed, and only the kind list is a named export of the store (DECISION_KINDS, to be aligned with the SO-A-05 build before signing). (b) The exact function names of the trust book (grant and revoke with a resolved actor) are those of the PG-W-21B amendment and are aligned before signing. (c) The proposer may be a person or operator as well as an agent or service; a proposal by a person still waits for an answer, and an operator may answer a proposal that it proposed (no two-person rule, which is a decision for ADR 5). (d) Evidence references on a proposed grant are references only and at most 8, as the record validator says; the external trust service is consulted at approval, never per contribution (PG-W-21B amendment), and this contract never calls it. BOUNDARIES. PG-W-21A.2 (the record, its signature block, verification level, reserved delegation, roots) and PG-W-21B (the book, GRANT_AUTHORITY, the marking overlay) are cited by id and not repeated; SO-A-05 (the decision workflow, seven states) is cited and its build is a dependency: this contract uses its states raised, approved, rejected and deferred by name and defines none; pairing is PG-W-21D; entitlement is PG-W-21E. Nothing here adds a role-by-action matrix or decides ADR 3, ADR 5, ADR 7 or SO-A-05, and the topology of work breakdown row 1.3.6 stays OPEN. Depends on contracts: SO-A-05 (built), the amended PG-W-21B and PG-W-21A.2. Base revision: 4db303071c67c32e2e5b3ecd508a10748b5b5a34, the memev main commit this spec was written against and the commit the red runs are judged at; the SO-A-05 build is applied on it before the build starts. The tests reach the modules by namespace import() inside each test with typeof asserts, so a missing export fails on an assertion and not at load. Owner decisions of 31 Oct 2026 apply: crdt-merge stays in its own repository; tiers are free core, Personal at $12/month or $120/year for up to 3 computers, and contact us above that.

tasks.title: An agent proposes a trust grant or revocation as a decision; only a person or operator answers; the answer is signed, logged and the only way a record is written
requirements: src/engine/federation/trust-propose.mjs (new) exports PROPOSAL_SCHEMA (memev-trust-proposal/1), ANSWER_NAMESPACE (memev-trust-approval), PROPOSAL_TTL_DAYS (14), proposeTrustChange, answerTrustChange and changeHash; nothing throws on bad input, each returns { ok: false, code, reason }; the module imports src/engine/identity.mjs and, for GRANT_AUTHORITY, the trust book module of PG-W-21B, and does not import src/engine/project-store.mjs or src/engine/merge.mjs

proposeTrustChange({ queue, actor, change, recommendation, at, validate }) requires a resolved actor (isResolvedActor of src/engine/identity.mjs) of any subject type that the identity model resolves for a credential, and takes the proposer from that actor, never from the change; it refuses a change whose kind is not grant or revoke, that names a personal scope, that carries a delegation block (delegation is reserved in the format and not accepted: ADR 8 clarification 8), more than 8 evidence references, or that the record validator of PG-W-21A.2 refuses (the validator is a parameter, validate, so the test needs no build of it); it raises one decision through queue.raise of kind trust.grant or trust.revoke holding the change, its changeHash, the proposer, the recommendation in the recommendation field only and the time, and returns the decision id; it has no book parameter and writes no trust record

answerTrustChange({ queue, book, actor, decision, answer, change_hash, sign, principal, at }) reads the decision through queue.read; only an actor whose subject type is permitted by GRANT_AUTHORITY (a person or an operator, provisional under ADR 5) may answer, an agent, service, device or node is refused with not_authorised; the answer is one of approve, reject and defer and is always explicit (the recommendation is never copied into it); an approve needs change_hash equal to the hash of the stored change, a decision still awaiting an answer and not older than PROPOSAL_TTL_DAYS, otherwise it is refused with changed, already_answered or expired

on approve the person's signature over the decision id, the change hash, the answer, the approver and the time is made with the caller's sign function in the namespace memev-trust-approval and kept with the result; the book is then called once, grant or revoke according to the kind, with the change and the approver's resolved actor as the actor, so the issuer of the record is the approver and never the proposer; the queue is settled approved; a book that refuses leaves the decision unanswered with the refusal logged; reject and defer settle the decision rejected or deferred, call no book method and write no record

every proposal and every answer appends an event to the operation log through a log the caller gives (trust.proposal.raised, trust.proposal.answered) with the decision id, the kind, the change hash, the proposer, the approver, the answer and, for an approval, the signature; an event holds references and hashes and never the content of a contribution, a token or a key

src/engine/project-store.mjs: the closed kind list of the decision entity of SO-A-05 (exported as DECISION_KINDS) gains trust.grant and trust.revoke; no other line of the store, the approval conflict rule or the replay changes; the file gains no import

docs/FEDERATION.md describes the proposal step (agents propose, the person or operator answers, the answer is signed, logged and the only way a record is written, a proposal is bound to its hash and expires after 14 days), says it is provisional under ADR 5 and adds no role-by-action matrix, and says that the external trust service is consulted at approval and never per contribution; no file of src, scripts or vendor changes but the new module and project-store.mjs; each red-green criterion runs only its own subtest whose name starts with T1-cNN: (source: the convention of SR-0.03.3 T1 requirement 8)
tasks.description: Repo: memev. Builds on the SO-A-05 build. The fixtures are an in-memory queue port with raise, read and settle, a fake trust book that records its grant and revoke calls and their actors, resolved actors made by resolveActor of src/engine/identity.mjs for a person, an operator, an agent and a service, a vault OpLog in a temporary directory, and a fake sign and verify pair that hashes the signed message. A stand-in of every subtest was run read-only at the base: each fails on ERR_ASSERTION.

criteria.statement: trust-propose.mjs exports PROPOSAL_SCHEMA, ANSWER_NAMESPACE (memev-trust-approval), PROPOSAL_TTL_DAYS 14, proposeTrustChange, answerTrustChange and changeHash; changeHash is the SHA-256 of the canonical change and is the same for equal changes and different for any changed field; DECISION_KINDS of src/engine/project-store.mjs holds trust.grant and trust.revoke beside the kinds it already had and the rest of its content is unchanged. The test fails before the change on an assertion, not on a load error or a TypeError, and passes after.

stop_rules: No weakening of an existing test, no raised timeout, no skip, no widened scope; if blocked, report what blocks and continue with the next independent task.
A criterion that cannot be checked from this repository is reported as unchecked, never marked as passing.
Anything outside the requirements of this task is not built, not stubbed and not defaulted in code; if the work seems to need it, stop and report what it needs.
A test_red_green command of this contract prints its whole output: it is never piped through tail or head, and never captures its output without printing it.

Stop and ask when the work would decide ADR 3, ADR 5, ADR 7 or SO-A-05, add a role-by-action matrix, pick the topology of work breakdown row 1.3.6, or touch the licence terms, the tier prices or the crdt-merge terms.
Stop and ask when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
Stop when the work would edit a signed spec or a signed contract: a signed id is superseded by a new id, never edited.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.

Stop and ask when the work would let any code path copy a recommendation into an answer, let a proposer answer for a person, write a trust record from the proposal step, or add a role-by-action matrix.
Stop and ask when the SO-A-05 build names the decision kind list or the queue differently from this spec: amend the spec before building, never bend the test.
